dialog.body: City of Newport Utilities, billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Good afternoon, Mr. Ferreira. My name is Fatima Moniz. I would like to inquire about a late fee that appeared on my water and sewer bill. I find it quite unacceptable, because I mailed that check on time.
Okay, Ms. Moniz, sorry about that. Let me pull you up. What's the service address on the account?
It is 256 Gidley Street. That is in the Fifth Ward. I have lived there for a good many years and I have never once been charged a penalty.
Got it, 256 Gidley. Give me a second here while it loads. [pause] Okay, I see the account. I'm showing a late charge on the most recent bill. What date did you mail the check?
I mailed it on the Friday before the due date. I remember specifically, because I took it to the post office myself. I did not leave it in the box at the curb.
Alright. And do you remember the check number, or what amount it was for?

The amount was one hundred and eighty-some dollars. I do not have the checkbook in front of me at this moment. Wait, I should say, I may be looking at the wrong statement. I also own a second property, a two-family on the other side of town, and the bills look very much alike.
Ah, okay. So two accounts. That happens a lot. Do you have the bill in your hand that shows the late fee?

I have two of them here on the table. One moment. [pause] This one says Gidley Street at the top. The late fee is on the other one, I believe. No, wait. Let me look again. Yes, I apologize, the late fee is on the one for the rental.
No problem at all. So the late fee isn't on Gidley, it's on the rental. What's the address on that one?

That would be 41 Hammond Street. I believe I wrote the check for Gidley Street twice, or perhaps I put the wrong account number on the memo line. I really cannot say. I am quite aggravated, because this is the sort of mix-up that costs me money.

I hear you. Let me look at both. [pause] Okay, so here's what I'm seeing. Gidley Street got a payment posted and it's current. The Hammond account shows the balance unpaid past the due date, and that's where the late charge came from. It looks like your payment went to Gidley, and it was a little more than what was owed there, so there's a credit sitting on that account.
So the money is there. It simply went to the wrong place.
Right, it's sitting in the wrong account. The payment came in under the Gidley account number, so the system applied it there. We can move that credit over to Hammond, that's something we can do.
And the late fee? I would like it removed. I did mail the check on time. The error was clerical, and the city has had my money the entire time.

Understood. I can't wipe the fee myself from this desk, but I can note the account with what happened and send a request for review. It goes to the supervisor. Usually when the payment was on time and it just landed on the wrong account, they take that into account. I can't promise, but that's how I'd explain it.
I would appreciate that. I would like it noted that this is the first time in many years, on either property.
Will do. I'll put that in the note. And I'll move the credit over so the Hammond balance gets covered. Might take a day or two to show up.

Thank you. Now, I would like to inquire about something else. If a balance remains after the transfer, can I pay it online tonight? City Hall will be closed by the time I am home, and I do not care to drive down there tomorrow.

Yes, you can pay online any time, day or night. There's a payment page on the city website, and you'd need the account number off the bill. There's also a drop box outside City Hall for checks, if you'd rather do that.
I see. And which account number do I use? The two bills look so similar that I fear I will do the same thing again.

Good question. Each bill has its own account number near the top, and the service address is printed right by it. Just make sure the number matches the address you want to pay. For Hammond, read the number off the Hammond bill, not the Gidley one.
Very well. I will lay them side by side and put a sticky note on each one. Perhaps that is what I should have done to begin with.
Sticky notes are great, honestly. Saves a lot of headaches.

Mr. Ferreira, I must apologize, there is a noise in the background. My clothes dryer buzzer keeps going off. It has been doing it on and off all afternoon, and I cannot get it to stop. It is dreadfully distracting.
No worries, I can't fix the dryer from here, but I get it. Go ahead and take care of it if you need to. I'm not going anywhere.
No, no, it can wait. It is only a buzzer. Now, would you be so kind as to read back what you will do, so that I am certain?

Sure. One, I'm moving the extra credit from the Gidley account over to the Hammond Street account. Two, I'm sending the late fee for review with a note that your check was mailed on time and went to the wrong account by mistake. Three, if any balance is left on Hammond after that, you can pay online anytime, using the account number from the Hammond bill.
That is correct. And will someone contact me regarding the late fee?
They'd likely adjust it on the account, and you'd see it on the next statement. If you want a call back, I can put a number on the note. Is the best number the one you're calling from?
Please use 401-555-0192. That is my cell phone. I do not always hear it, so I would ask that they leave a message.
Got it, 401-555-0192, leave a message. Anything else I can help with today?
No, that is all. I am still rather displeased that it took a late fee to reveal the error, but I appreciate your patience, Mr. Ferreira.
Totally fair. Sorry for the hassle, Ms. Moniz. Have a good rest of your Tuesday, and happy new year in advance.
Thank you. Good afternoon.
